sentences.en: So they have, you know, they, they reject all titles.
sentences.zh: 所以他们，你知道的，他们拒绝所有的头衔。

sentences.en: They reject any claim that men might have to a kind of superiority over women.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝承认男性对女性拥有任何优越性。

sentences.en: So kind of a very radical sense of gender equality.
sentences.zh: 因此这是一种非常激进的性别平等观念。

sentences.en: Um, they're very austere in their personal habits, which is a crucial part of what makes them, um, influential almost immediately.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在个人习惯上非常简朴，这是他们几乎立刻就能产生影响力的关键部分。

sentences.en: People see them as kind of saintly figures.
sentences.zh: 人们将他们视为某种圣洁的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, and they are very, very into expressing these views through a kind of activism.
sentences.zh: 而且他们非常热衷于通过某种积极行动来表达这些观点。

sentences.en: So the famous thing that they do is, is refuse to take their hats off.
sentences.zh: 他们做的最著名的举动之一，就是拒绝脱帽。

sentences.en: That is unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: That's absolutely shameful behavior, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是无耻的行为，汤姆。

sentences.en: Um, shocking subversion of, of, of everything that...
sentences.zh: 嗯，对……一切传统令人震惊的颠覆。

sentences.en: Well, actually, you know what?
sentences.zh: 好吧，其实你知道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we're joking about it, but in the, if you're in the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在开玩笑，但如果你身处

sentences.zh: 1650年代或1660年代，不脱帽可是件大事，对吧？

sentences.en: It's shocking.
sentences.zh: 太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: Completely shocking.
sentences.zh: 完全令人震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Alec Ryrie, who's a brilliant historian of Protestantism, wrote a wonderful book about it.
sentences.zh: 新教的杰出历史学家亚历克·赖里（Alec Ryrie）曾写过一本关于这方面的精彩书籍。

sentences.en: He tells a story of, um, a servant girl called Elizabeth Andrews, who is, you know, she works in the house of, uh, Lord Newport.
sentences.zh: 他讲了一个关于，嗯，一个叫伊丽莎白·安德鲁斯的侍女的故事，你知道的，她在，呃，纽波特勋爵的府邸工作。

sentences.en: So he's not just, you know, he's not just her social superior.
sentences.zh: 所以他不仅仅是，你知道的，不只是在社会地位上高她一等。

sentences.en: He's an aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 他是个贵族。

sentences.en: And when she is serving guests at table, she refuses to curtsy to them.
sentences.zh: 当她在餐桌旁侍候客人时，她拒绝向他们行屈膝礼。

sentences.en: And she, the guests are kind of more amused by this, I think, than outrage.
sentences.zh: 而且她，我觉得客人们对这事的反应更多是觉得好笑，而不是被激怒。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so shocking that they, they can't even be offended by it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太让人震惊了，以至于他们甚至无法为此感到生气。

sentences.en: It's like she turned out with no clothes on or something.
sentences.zh: 就像她光着身子跑出来或者别的什么一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, we'll come to that in a minute.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们一会儿再谈这个。

sentences.en: But, and they offer her 20 pounds to curtsy.
sentences.zh: 但是，他们给了她20英镑让她行屈膝礼。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a hell of a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那可是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And she refuses.
sentences.zh: 而她拒绝了。

sentences.en: And she says, I durst not do it for all honor belongeth to God.
sentences.zh: 她说，我不敢这么做，因为所有的荣耀都归于上帝。

sentences.en: So she turns down 20 pounds, refuses to curtsy.
sentences.zh: 所以她拒绝了20英镑，拒绝行屈膝礼。

sentences.en: Now you mentioned the nudity.
sentences.zh: 现在你提到了裸体。

sentences.en: Quakers in the, in the 1650s are quite into nudity.
sentences.zh: 1650年代的贵格会教徒对裸体相当热衷。

sentences.en: You amaze me.
sentences.zh: 你可真让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: And they're doing this, not like the Adamites who are also part of the, the swirl of the religious times who were doing it because they say, you know, you should try and get back
sentences.zh: 他们这样做，不像亚当派那样——亚当派也是那个宗教风潮激荡时期的一部分，他们这样做是因为他们说，你知道的，你应该试着回到

sentences.en: to the primordial innocence before the fall.
sentences.zh: 堕落之前的原始纯真状态。

sentences.en: Quakers are doing this as an, as a kind of activist stunt.
sentences.zh: 贵格会教徒这样做是一种，某种激进主义的特技。

sentences.en: So they are saying that they're doing it to highlight the way in which priests, prelates, Presbyterians are hypocrites and that they are stripping off their clothes to
sentences.zh: 所以他们说他们这样做是为了突出牧师、高级神职人员、长老会教徒的虚伪本质，他们脱下衣服是为了

sentences.en: kind of demonstrate the way in which.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上展示这种状态。

sentences.en: They should be stripping off the priest's clothes really.
sentences.zh: 其实他们本该脱掉牧师的衣服才对。

sentences.en: I would have said, but anyway, there you go.
sentences.zh: 我本来会这么说的，不过不管怎样，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, well, but also it's targeting Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，但这也把矛头对准了克伦威尔。

sentences.en: So there's a, there's a Quaker in 1654 who walks through the streets of Oxford, absolutely naked.
sentences.zh: 所以在1654年，有一个贵格会教徒赤身裸体地走过牛津的街道。

sentences.en: Um, and he's doing this as a, to, to make a kind of visual prophecy that in times, but very soon Cromwell will be stripped of his.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他这么做是为了，做出一种视觉上的预言：在不久的将来，克伦威尔的权力将被剥夺。

sentences.en: That's, I mean, you know, my views on Oliver Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 那就是，我的意思是，你知道我对克伦威尔的看法。

sentences.en: He is not a man.
sentences.zh: 他可不是那种人。

sentences.en: I imagine that would in a million years walk through the streets of Oxford naked.
sentences.zh: 我想他有一百万年也不可能赤身裸体走过牛津的街道。

sentences.en: Is he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: No, but he is quite tolerant of the Quakers.
sentences.zh: 不，但他对贵格会教徒相当宽容。

sentences.en: Is he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Because he is, because, you know, I said that there's a kind of a radical gender equality by the standards of the age.
sentences.zh: 因为他是，因为，你知道的，我刚才说过，按那个时代的标准来看，他们有一种激进的性别平等。

sentences.en: So women are as ready to preach this message as men.
sentences.zh: 所以女性和男性一样随时准备宣讲这个信息。

sentences.en: And one of them walks into his private quarters in Whitehall.
sentences.zh: 其中一人走进了他在白厅的私人住所。

sentences.en: Clothed or unclothed?
sentences.zh: 穿着衣服还是没穿？

sentences.en: Clothed.
sentences.zh: 穿着衣服。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But she, she sits down next to, next to Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 但她，她在克伦威尔旁边坐了下来。

sentences.en: She kind of bursts into his bedroom, sits down next to him, calls him a dunghill.
sentences.zh: 她可以说是闯入了他的卧室，在他旁边坐下，骂他是粪堆。

sentences.en: And then basically spends an hour haranguing him, urging him to become a Quaker.
sentences.zh: 然后基本上花了一个小时痛斥他，敦促他成为一名贵格会教徒。

sentences.en: And Cromwell, to give him credit, I mean, he sits there and this, you know, hears her out and then has her escorted very politely out.
sentences.zh: 而克伦威尔，平心而论，我的意思是，他就坐在那儿，你知道的，听她把话说完，然后非常客气地让人把她护送出去。

sentences.en: So there's no, no kind of comeback.
sentences.zh: 所以没有什么，没有什么报复性的举动。

sentences.en: That's nice.
sentences.zh: 这挺不错的。

sentences.en: And amazingly, there's another, another woman who's a former housemaid.
sentences.zh: 神奇的是，还有另一个，另一个女人，她曾是一名女佣。

sentences.en: She goes to America.
sentences.zh: 她去了美洲。

sentences.en: So she's one of the very first Quakers to arrive in America.
sentences.zh: 所以她是第一批抵达美洲的贵格会教徒之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And she's treated very, very badly by the Pilgrim Fathers out there.
sentences.zh: 她在那里面对那里的清教徒先辈时，受到了非常非常糟糕的对待。

sentences.en: So the Puritans in New
sentences.zh: 所以新英格兰的清教徒

sentences.en: England, she's whipped and then she's deported.
sentences.zh: 鞭打她，然后把她驱逐出境。

sentences.en: So what she does is she goes to, she crosses, she goes back to Europe and she, she goes to, um, to meet the Sultan, the Ottoman Sultan.
sentences.zh: 所以她做的是，她去，她横渡大海，回到了欧洲，然后她去，嗯，去拜访苏丹，奥斯曼苏丹。

sentences.en: She meets him at Adrianople, at Ian.
sentences.zh: 她在阿德里安堡见到了他，在伊安。

sentences.en: I can't see the Ottomans caring for being addressed by naked people, calling them dunghills.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象奥斯曼人会介意被一群赤身裸体、管他们叫粪堆的人搭话。

sentences.en: Well, again, the Sultan is much more tolerant, like Cromwell is much more tolerant than the, uh, the Puritans in New England.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还是那句话，苏丹要宽容得多，就像克伦威尔比新英格兰的清教徒宽容得多一样。

sentences.en: Here's her out.
sentences.zh: 他听她把话说完了。

sentences.en: And the woman says that he was very noble unto me.
sentences.zh: 那个女人说他对她非常高尚。

sentences.en: So there is, I think, a sense in which people are willing to, uh, whether it's Cromwell
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，在某种意义上，人们愿意，无论是克伦威尔

sentences.en: or the Ottoman Sultan are willing to, you know, these people are so extraordinary that they're
sentences.zh: 还是奥斯曼苏丹都愿意，你知道的，这些人是如此非凡，以至于他们

sentences.en: almost, you know, you, they're almost kind of figures of fun perhaps, but so earnest, so brave mixed in with that is a sense that they are to be respected.
sentences.zh: 几乎，你知道的，你几乎觉得他们有点像搞笑人物，但他们又是如此真诚、勇敢，夹杂着一种应当受到尊重的敬意。

sentences.en: But having said that Quakers can go too far.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，贵格会教徒也可能会走得太远。

sentences.en: So the most notorious example of that is 1656, um, a Quaker by the name of James Naylor, who gets so carried away with this sense that he's possessed by the spirit that he actually
sentences.zh: 其中最臭名昭著的例子发生在1656年，嗯，一个名叫詹姆斯·内勒的贵格会教徒，他被自己被精神附体的感觉冲昏了头脑，以至于他竟然

sentences.en: identifies with Jesus.
sentences.zh: 把自己当成了耶稣。

sentences.en: And on Palm Sunday, he simulates Jesus's entry into Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 在棕枝主日那天，他模拟了耶稣进入耶路撒冷的场景。

sentences.en: Um, you know, with people laying down palms in front of him, um, he, he does it into Bristol.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，人们在他面前铺上棕榈枝，嗯，他，他进入了布里斯托尔。

sentences.en: So casting
sentences.zh: 所以把

sentences.en: Bristol as the new Jerusalem, and this goes down terribly badly.
sentences.zh: 布里斯托尔当作新的耶路撒冷，这引发了极坏的反响。

sentences.en: And although Cromwell doesn't approve of the fate that's visited on him, he suffers horribly.
sentences.zh: 尽管克伦威尔并不赞成降临在他身上的命运，但他还是遭受了可怕的折磨。

sentences.en: So he has a red hot iron kind of goes through his tongue, leaves a hole in it.
sentences.zh: 所以一根烧红的铁条穿过他的舌头，留下了一个洞。

sentences.en: He has B branded on his forehead for blasphemer.
sentences.zh: 他的额头上被烙上了代表亵渎者的字母B。

sentences.en: He does two years hard labor.
sentences.zh: 他做了两年的苦工。

sentences.en: So the Quakers are kind of steering close to the wind and sometimes they, horrible things happen to them.
sentences.zh: 所以贵格会教徒有时是在玩火，有时可怕的事情会降临到他们头上。

sentences.en: But what happens in the wake of the restoration is that that kind of that spirit fire, if you want to put it like that, starts to fade.
sentences.zh: 但在君主制复辟之后发生的事情是，那种精神之火，如果你愿意这么说的话，开始逐渐消逝了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so Benjamin Lay is born into a world where Quakers are a good deal less radical in their kind of public manifestations of the spirit than they had been.
sentences.zh: 所以本杰明·莱伊出生于这样一个世界：贵格会教徒在公开展示信仰方面，远没有以前那么激进了。

sentences.en: But the thing about Lay is that he kind of holds true to that primal sense of radicalism.
sentences.zh: 但莱伊的特点在于，他坚守着那种最初的激进主义精神。

sentences.en: Were his parents very keen?
sentences.zh: 他的父母很热心吗？

sentences.en: They were.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's, they seem to have been a direct influence on him.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎对他的影响非常直接。

sentences.en: So tell me, you said he was short.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我，你刚才说他很矮？

sentences.en: He's, um, four foot seven and he has a very large head and he's a hunchback and he stands in a peculiar manner.
sentences.zh: 他，嗯，身高四尺七寸，脑袋非常大，还是个驼背，站姿很奇特。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, it sounds like, frankly, a slightly camp manner.
sentences.zh: 嗯，坦白说，听起来有点娘娘腔的姿态。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So a description of him that was written by, um, a man called Roberts Vokes writing in the
sentences.zh: 所以关于他的描述是由，嗯，一个叫罗伯茨·沃克斯的人在

sentences.en: early 19th century, who was, um, an abolitionist in Philadelphia and a Quaker and wrote a biography of Benjamin Lay that most of our information about him comes from.
sentences.zh: 19世纪初写下的，他当时是费城的一名废奴主义者兼贵格会教徒，他写了一本关于本杰明·莱伊的传记，我们关于他的大部分信息都来源于此。

sentences.en: And he says, yes, he was hunchbacked with a projecting chest below which his body became much contracted.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，他是个驼背，胸部前突，突出的胸部下方身体急剧收缩。

sentences.en: His legs were so slender as to appear, almost unequal to the purpose of supporting him, diminutive as his frame was in comparison with the ordinary size of the human stature.
sentences.zh: 他的双腿细得几乎快要支撑不住身体，与人类正常的身高相比，他的骨架小得可怜。

sentences.en: A habit he had contracted of standing in a twisted position with one hand resting upon his left hip added to the effect
sentences.zh: 他习惯于以一种扭曲的姿势站立，一只手搭在左臀上，这种习惯

sentences.en: produced by a large white beard that for many years had not been shaved contributed to render his figure perfectly unique.
sentences.zh: 加上他那多年未曾刮过的大白胡子，让他的外形显得极其独特。

sentences.en: So, so a striking figure and he, you know, his parents are humble.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个引人注目的人物，而且你知道的，他的父母出身卑微。

sentences.en: So he's an autodidact.
sentences.zh: 所以他是自学成才的。

sentences.en: Um, so he works variously as a shepherd, as a glover, works in agriculture, works as a sailor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他做过各种工作，当过牧羊人、手套匠、干过农业，还当过水手。

sentences.en: And in the course of one of his, um, voyages, he visits Syria.
sentences.zh: 在他的一次，嗯，航海途中，他访问了叙利亚。

sentences.en: He could have met up with that Quaker woman who went to, uh, Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 他本可以遇到那个去过，呃，君士坦丁堡的贵格会女性。

sentences.en: Well, it's a bit, yeah, it's later, it's several decades after that, but all the time as Quakers do, he is reading and reading and reading.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有点，是的，时间要晚一些，在几十年之后，但像所有贵格会教徒一样，他一直在不断地阅读、阅读、再阅读。

sentences.en: And his sense that the spirit is on him is informing his reading.
sentences.zh: 他那种感到神灵附体的意识一直在滋养着他的阅读。

sentences.en: So he loves Milton.
sentences.zh: 所以他热爱弥尔顿。

sentences.en: He said, it's typically, he said to present to George the first with one of Milton's tracts.
sentences.zh: 据说，他曾把弥尔顿的一本小册子呈献给乔治一世。

sentences.en: So obviously the idea of presenting a king with Milton, who was a famous defender of regicide is very Benjamin Lay.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，把弥尔顿——这位著名的弑君者辩护人——的作品呈献给一位国王，非常符合本杰明·莱伊的风格。

sentences.en: Also a German king whose English is famously not very good.
sentences.zh: 而且还是个英语出了名不怎么样的德国国王。

sentences.en: I mean, he's not going to be dipping into Milton.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他根本不可能去读弥尔顿。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: So that's probably why he got away with it.
sentences.zh: 所以这大概就是他为什么能蒙混过关的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And Benjamin Lay feels that the Quakers, maybe 50 years after they'd first started appearing,
sentences.zh: 本杰明·莱伊觉得，贵格会教徒在他们开始出现的大约50年后，

sentences.en: are starting to become a bit Presbyterian, a bit Anglican in that they're starting to get a hierarchy of elders.
sentences.zh: 开始变得有点像长老会和英国国教了，因为他们开始建立长老等级制度了。

sentences.en: Oh, they're selling out.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们背叛了初心。

sentences.en: They're kind of selling out.
sentences.zh: 他们有点向世俗妥协了。

sentences.en: And he's very opposed to this.
sentences.zh: 他对此坚决反对。

sentences.en: And he starts to disrupt
sentences.zh: 他开始扰乱

sentences.en: Quaker meetings, objecting.
sentences.zh: 贵格会聚会，提出抗议。

sentences.en: And, and Vokes has this description of this.
sentences.zh: 沃克斯对这段经历有这样的描述。

sentences.en: He says his temper was violent, but it was always excited for mercy's sake.
sentences.zh: 他说他的脾气很暴躁，但他的怒火总是为了慈悲而被点燃。

sentences.en: And in behalf of those who dared not assert their own rights.
sentences.zh: 是为了那些不敢维护自身权利的人挺身而出。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，他在推特上绝对是个噩梦。

sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He'd be throwing cans of soup over paintings and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他肯定会把一罐罐汤往名画上泼之类的。

sentences.en: All that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: All that kind of thing.
